_note: Reference bands for the metrics KG2 observes. Standard published adult ranges, cited per row, applied to synthetic data. They exist so 'is this value inside its band' is a graph fact rather than a constant in Python, and so a second member with age- or sex-adjusted bands needs no code change. The copilot reports values against these bands and names what sits outside them; it does not interpret, diagnose, or advise.

metrics.name: Sleep
metrics.reference: Her own stated target is 7+ hours on weeknights (goals[] goal_sleep); general adult guidance is 7-9 h. This is the one band drawn from the member's goal rather than a population range, which is why goal_sleep can hang measured_by off it.

metrics.name: Resting heart rate
metrics.reference: Adult resting heart rate is conventionally 60-100 bpm. Only the upper bound is recorded: values below 60 are common in trained adults, so a two-sided band would flag her 58 bpm as abnormal when it is favourable. This row is why MetricDirection exists separately from the band.

metrics.name: Heart rate variability
metrics.reference: RMSSD varies by an order of magnitude across healthy adults and by age. No population band is defensible, so none is authored — only change against her own baseline is meaningful. Left deliberately empty rather than filled with a plausible-looking number.

metrics.name: Body weight
metrics.reference: No target weight is recorded in any of her goals, so there is nothing to measure against. A band here would be invented.

metrics.name: LDL cholesterol
metrics.reference: Optimal LDL is under 100 mg/dL; 100-129 is near-optimal. Her 118 sits outside the optimal band, which is the only lab value in this sample that does so on the high side.

metrics.name: HDL cholesterol
metrics.reference: 50 mg/dL or above is the conventional threshold for women; 40 for men. Sex-specific, which is the case that justifies keeping bands as data rather than constants.

metrics.name: Triglycerides
metrics.reference: Normal fasting triglycerides are under 150 mg/dL.

metrics.name: HbA1c
metrics.reference: Under 5.7% is normal; 5.7-6.4% is the prediabetic range.

metrics.name: Vitamin D
metrics.reference: Sufficiency is 30 ng/mL or above; 20-29 is insufficient. Her 28 sits just below, and it is the only value in the panel outside its band on the low side.

metrics.name: Ferritin
metrics.reference: Adult female reference range is 15-150 ng/mL. Genuinely two-sided: both deficiency and overload matter, which is what BAND means and what neither HIGHER_BETTER nor LOWER_BETTER can express.

metrics.name: C-reactive protein
metrics.reference: High-sensitivity CRP under 3.0 mg/L corresponds to low cardiovascular risk.

metrics.name: Body fat
metrics.reference: Acceptable range for women aged 40-59 is roughly 21-33%. Age- and sex-specific, so the band belongs with the member's data rather than in code.

metrics.name: Lean mass
metrics.reference: No population band; absolute lean mass depends on height and frame. Direction of travel is what a strength goal cares about.

metrics.name: Fat mass
metrics.reference: Derived from body weight and body fat percentage, both of which carry their own rows. Kept as its own metric because the scan reports it, and dropping a reported value would make the panel look incomplete.

metrics.name: Bone density Z-score
metrics.reference: A Z-score of -2.0 or above is within the expected range for age. Z rather than T because she is premenopausal.

metrics.name: Visceral fat area
metrics.reference: 100 cm2 is the commonly cited threshold above which metabolic risk rises.

metrics.name: Weekly completion
metrics.reference: Her plan is 4 sessions a week (preferences.training_days_per_week), so 100% means every planned session was done. The band is 100 rather than a softer number because the metric is already normalised against her own plan — anything below it is a session she was scheduled for and did not do.
